decision.summary: The Federal Reserve decided to hold the federal funds rate steady at 0 to 1/4 percent and maintain its supportive monetary policy stance.

changes.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in June suggests that economic activity decelerated somewhat over the first half of this year.
changes.explanation: The Fed noted that economic growth slowed down during the first half of the year compared to its earlier view.

changes.quote: Growth in employment has been slow in recent months, and the unemployment rate remains elevated.
changes.explanation: The language on job creation was downgraded to show that hiring has been slow recently.

changes.quote: Inflation has declined since earlier this year, mainly reflecting lower prices of crude oil and gasoline, and longer-term inflation expectations have remained stable.
changes.explanation: The Fed acknowledged that inflation dropped due to cheaper oil and gas prices.

changes.quote: The Committee also decided to continue through the end of the year its program to extend the average maturity of its holdings of securities as announced in June, and it is maintaining its existing policy of reinvesting principal payments from its holdings of agency debt and agency mortgage-backed securities in agency mortgage-backed securities.
changes.explanation: The Fed formally integrated its decision to continue its maturity extension program through the end of the year.

changes.quote: The Committee will closely monitor incoming information on economic and financial developments and will provide additional accommodation as needed to promote a stronger economic recovery and sustained improvement in labor market conditions in a context of price stability.
changes.explanation: The Fed shifted its wording to emphasize that it is ready to provide more support if the economy and labor market need it.

tone_quotes.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in June suggests that economic activity decelerated somewhat over the first half of this year.
Growth in employment has been slow in recent months, and the unemployment rate remains elevated.

The Committee will closely monitor incoming information on economic and financial developments and will provide additional accommodation as needed to promote a stronger economic recovery and sustained improvement in labor market conditions in a context of price stability.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 12.34% APR costs about $51.42 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 1.56% and moved +5 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 3.53% would rise by about $8.40 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 8.2%, and employers added an average of 88k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 1.7% over the past year (June 2012); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.8%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 1.8% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +1 bp on the day.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved 0.05% on the day.

whats_next: The statement signals that the Federal Reserve will likely maintain its exceptionally low interest rate target at least through late 2014. Additionally, an educational forecast model gives a 73% probability that the Fed will hold rates again at its next meeting.

citations.detail: In particular, the Committee decided today to keep the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent and currently anticipates that economic conditions--including low rates of resource utilization and a subdued outlook for inflation over the medium run--are likely to warrant exceptionally low levels for the federal funds rate at least through late 2014.
